title: Certificate Symbol Under the Last Head
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $w,u$ be Boolean words, and choose a saved configuration of $M$ on input $w$, a semantic state $q$, a natural number $i\le |w|$, and an integer offset $j$. The symbol under the head of the evaluator's last work tape in the corresponding canonical evaluation configuration is the content of the certificate buffer $u$ at offset $j$.
hypotheses_covered: finite Boolean machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes
replaced:
Let $u$ be a certificate word and $j \in \mathbb{Z}$. In every canonical
evaluation configuration with certificate $u$ and certificate head at offset $j$,
the symbol read by the last work head is the cell of the buffer tape of $u$ at
offset $j$, that is, the $j$-th bit of $u$ when $0 \le j < |u|$ and the blank
otherwise.
